errors.english: do not eat without first assessing the amount of lentils or pulse provided for the illness
errors.why: This is the sekhiya rule against covering the curry/sauce (with rice) out of greed for more, illness excepted; nothing about assessing portions provided for an illness.

errors.english: Not in a place of violent robbery where the current of safety is reversed. These instructions up to the word "ten"
errors.why: The rule is not to scoop/draw water against the current of a violent, sweeping stream; mi bcu is 'do not draw (water)', not the numeral ten, and there is no robbery.

fix.find: Not in a place of violent robbery where the current of safety is reversed. These instructions up to the word "ten"
fix.replace: Do not draw water against the current of a violent, sweeping stream. These instructions up to "do not draw water"

errors.english: do not complain that the food is too hot or too cold, and do not spit while eating
errors.why: The gloss says only: do not disparage the food as too bitter (kha), too cold and so on; there is no rule about spitting.

fix.find: do not complain that the food is too hot or too cold, and do not spit while eating
fix.replace: do not disparage the food, saying it is too bitter, too cold and so forth

errors.english: Do not teach while walking in front to one who is following behind.
errors.why: As in the parallel rules (instrumental = teacher, la = listener), it forbids one coming behind from teaching one who goes in front.

fix.find: Do not teach while walking in front to one who is following behind.
fix.replace: Do not teach while following behind to one who is walking in front.

note: Most of the eating and teaching rules are rendered correctly, but several rules are misread, and in one the teacher and listener are reversed.

errors.english: the fourth-class (dha) becomes the first-class (da) as if the change had not occurred
errors.why: The rule makes the initial third-class consonant of such a root its fourth: initial d becomes dh (duh > dhuk), not dh > d.

fix.find: the fourth-class (dha) becomes the first-class (da) as if the change had not occurred
fix.replace: the initial third-class consonant becomes its fourth, so the initial (da) becomes (dha)

errors.english: (godhukkamyati) he desires a milk-cow
errors.why: godhuk (go-duh) is a milker of cows, not a milk-cow.

note: Follows the grammatical derivations reasonably well, but the dh-substitution rule is stated backwards and some example glosses are guesses.

errors.english: the monk who served the teachings of the Conqueror of All [note: original: "Tathagata"]
errors.why: Thams cad zil gyis gnon pa is the proper name of the Tathāgata Sarvābhibhū, and zhal ta byed pa is the monk acting as steward in his teaching.

fix.find: the monk who served the teachings of the Conqueror of All [note: original: "Tathagata"]
fix.replace: the monk who served as steward in the teaching of the Tathāgata Sarvābhibhū

errors.english: Furthermore, through the faults of the mind, one becomes like ashes.
errors.why: A mental fault reduces (the roots of virtue) to ashes; it is not the person who becomes ashes.

note: The sutra quotation and verses are faithful, but a buddha's proper name is translated as an epithet.
A faithful rendering of the first-bhūmi purifications, the eight mental attentions of the second bhūmi, and the Buddha-field gloss.

errors.english: The phrase "by the perceiver"
errors.why: Tshor ba po is the one who experiences feeling (vedanā); this links Ratnasambhava to the feeling aggregate, which 'perceiver' obscures.

errors.english: (Arolik) the seed syllable or name associated with the Lotus Family
errors.why: Ārolik is an epithet of Amitābha in the Nāmasaṃgīti, not a seed syllable.

note: The commentary on the family epithets reads well, with some loose glossing of the aggregate correspondences.

errors.english:
With fifty vital breaths, three breaths,
And its quarters
errors.why: The figure is fifty prāṇas plus three and three-quarter breaths; the 'three quarters' is lost.

errors.english:
In the southeast and in the northwest,
In the east and in the west,
errors.why: The Tibetan names the four elemental maṇḍalas (fire, wind, Mahendra/earth, water), not compass directions.

fix.find:
In the southeast and in the northwest,
In the east and in the west,
fix.replace:
Through fire and through wind,
Through Mahendra and through water,

errors.english:
The eastern will bring a kingdom,
The western wealth,
The southeastern death,
And the northwestern the diminution of wealth.
errors.why: The results are given per element: Mahendra brings kingship, water the accomplishment of aims, fire death, and wind the exhaustion of wealth.

fix.find:
The eastern will bring a kingdom,
The western wealth,
The southeastern death,
And the northwestern the diminution of wealth.
fix.replace:
Through Mahendra one becomes a king,
Through water one's aims are accomplished,
Through fire comes death,
And through wind wealth is exhausted.

note: The time-unit and breath calculus is accurate; the Sampuṭa quotation is rendered with compass directions where the Tibetan has elements.

errors.english: 2. by activity
errors.why: The second category is cessation by exhaustion (zad pa, as taken up below: ཟད་པས་འགོག་པ); las is the ablative marker, not 'activity'.

errors.english: there are four types, though that cessation cannot be described in any other way.
errors.why: This opens a tetralemma: the first of the four is that cessation cannot be said to be other, followed on the next side by not-other, both, and neither.

fix.find: there are four types, though that cessation cannot be described in any other way.
fix.replace: there are four, namely: that cessation cannot be said to be other;

note: The four-truths exposition is sound, but one item of the thirteenfold list is misread and the opening of the tetralemma is missed.

errors.english: He pleased seven hundred and twenty-seven [note: buddhas].
errors.why: Continuing སྟོང་ཕྲག་བདུན་ཅུ་ from the previous side, the number is seventy-seven thousand buddhas.

fix.find: He pleased seven hundred and twenty-seven [note: buddhas].

errors.english: residing in the realm of majesty
errors.why: Puṣya was absorbed in the meditative attainment of the fire element (tejodhātu), the well-known story of the Bodhisattva standing on one foot.

fix.find: residing in the realm of majesty
fix.replace: absorbed in meditation on the fire element (tejodhātu)

note: The kalpa and buddha counts are mostly right, but one count is wrong and the samādhi in the Puṣya episode is misidentified.

errors.english: There is also no connection between the definition of emptiness and that which arises from it, because it is eternal.
errors.why: The text denies a causal relation (tadutpatti, the relation characterized as arising from it) between emptiness and things, because emptiness is permanent; mtshan nyid qualifies the relation.

fix.find: There is also no connection between the definition of emptiness and that which arises from it, because it is eternal.
fix.replace: Nor is there between emptiness and things a relation of the kind characterized as arising from it (tadutpatti), because emptiness is permanent.

errors.english: Because things [note: as independent entities] do not exist, emptiness is not an effect
errors.why: Emptiness is itself a non-entity, and so is not an effect; the claim is not that things do not exist.

errors.english: The very nature of birth, occurring in the beginningless cycle of existence for those with an obsession with things, is a cause of delusion
errors.why: The subject is the clinging to things, which by nature arises beginninglessly in saṃsāra; that clinging is the intoxicating poison, not 'the nature of birth'.

note: The commentary's word-connections are followed, but the argument about the relation between emptiness and things is misconstrued in several places.

errors.english: it is not expressed as being "possessed of the very basis upon which that basis is obtained," which refers to its essential nature.
errors.why: The Tibetan says that in 'whoever has obtained a basis is possessed of that very basis' the word evidently means 'with that essence'; there is no negation.

fix.find: it is not expressed as being "possessed of the very basis upon which that basis is obtained," which refers to its essential nature.
fix.replace: in "whoever has obtained a basis is possessed of that very basis," it evidently means "possessed of that essence."

errors.english: (fetters) proclivities or latent afflictions
errors.why: Kun tu sbyor ba is saṃyojana (fetter), distinct from anuśaya (latent proclivity).

note: A sound rendering of the five senses of vastu and the upādāna-skandha compound, except for a negation added in the first sense.
